GEENI.method_comparison: No algorithm, loss, aggregation, sharing or graph correction conclusion is adopted. Existing identity is not counted as new discovery.

HyperparameterEnsembles.application_limit: Scoped methods concern image classification architectures. No graph result, reproduced quality, code behavior or optimizer-universal theorem is adopted.
HyperparameterEnsembles.citation: Wenzel, Snoek, Tran and Jenatton, Hyperparameter Ensembles for Robustness and Uncertainty Quantification, arXiv:2006.13570v3
HyperparameterEnsembles.closest_prior_relation: Shared dense ensembles with private fast factors, hyperparameter/optimization diversity and a separate fast-factor step scale are direct antecedents to the generic learning-trajectory idea. The scoped text does not state a preserved-complete-initial-function gauge ensemble or a graph-conditioned error-correction construction.
HyperparameterEnsembles.fixed_init_hyper_ensemble: Section3 varies hyperparameters at fixed parameter initialization to isolate that diversity source. It greedily selects models with replacement using a declared score such as validation log likelihood.
HyperparameterEnsembles.hyper_batch_layer: Eq7 shares dense W and Delta while each member has r,s,u,v factors and bias terms; a learned embedding of member hyperparameters modulates the Delta term. Efficient batched prediction is retained.
HyperparameterEnsembles.hyper_deep_ensemble: Algorithm1 first selects a hyperparameter row, then trains selected configurations across random initializations and reselects from that stratified collection.
HyperparameterEnsembles.optimization_and_initialization: D.1 uses model SGD with Nesterov0.9, Adam for hyperparameter tuning, Gaussian rank-one factor entries around1, an explicit fast-weight learning-rate multiplier2.0, and no rank-factor regularization in the described setup. The source uses Gaussian notation N(1,0.5)/N(1,1); this scout does not resolve its variance-versus-standard-deviation convention.
HyperparameterEnsembles.selection_and_distribution_training: An alternating validation objective adapts distribution bounds with an entropy term. Bounded independent log-uniform distributions and prediction at their means are stated in Section4.2. This validation recipe is not adopted.
HyperparameterEnsembles.training_objective: Eqs8–9 introduce one hyperparameter distribution per member and an expected training objective. Section4.2 permits ensemble CE or mean ensemble-member CE; the authors state they use the latter.
